extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for claiming the benefit/priority of earlier U.S. (provisional and nonprovisional) applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, and 365(c). Covers copendency, required references, timing, correction, deletion, and petition procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copendency requirement for 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c) benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: When a later-filed application is claiming the benefit of a prior-filed nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c), the later-filed application must be copending with the prior application or with an intermediate nonprovisional application similarly entitled to the benefit of the filing date of the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copendency is satisfied if the later-filed application is filed before (A) patenting of the prior application; (B) abandonment of the prior application; or (C) termination of proceedings in the prior application. If the prior application issues as a patent, filing on the same date or before the patent issues is sufficient (applicants encouraged to file continuing applications no later than the date the issue fee is paid). If the prior application is abandoned, the later-filed application must be filed before abandonment. If not copending, the later-filed application is not entitled to the earlier filing date and prior art is determined from the later filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve-month filing rule for provisional benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application that directly claims the benefit of a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) must be filed within 12 months after the filing date of the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 12-month anniversary falls on a weekend or federal holiday in D.C., the nonprovisional may be filed on the next succeeding business day. If not filed within 12 months, an intermediate nonprovisional filed within 12 months that itself claims the provisional may preserve benefit, but that intermediate must be clearly identified. Failure to timely file directly claiming a provisional will render the direct claim improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific reference requirement (first sentence(s) or ADS) under 37 CFR 1.78
rubrics_metrics.description: The later-filed application must contain a specific reference to the prior application appearing as the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title (preferably as a separate paragraph) and/or in an application data sheet (ADS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specific reference is only in the ADS, the benefit claim information appears on the front page but not in the first sentence(s) of the specification. A reference submitted after filing cannot include an incorporation by reference of the prior application unless that incorporation was presented upon filing. If the reference is missing or improperly made, the Office may not recognize the benefit claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of prior nonprovisional by application number and relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, and 365(c) must identify the prior nonprovisional application by application number (or international application number and date) and indicate the relationship between the applications (continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement must include both the application number and the relationship (e.g., “This application is a continuation of prior Application No. ---, filed ---.”). A claim that merely states "claims the benefit of Application No. ---" or omits the relationship does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78(a)(2)(i). The relationship terms are exclusive and must be specified for each application in a chain where multiple prior applications are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not specify relationship for provisional claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming benefit to a prior provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), the relationship (continuation/divisional/CIP) is not required and should not be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not state that the nonprovisional is a "continuation" of a provisional or claim 120 benefit to a provisional; doing so may create ambiguity between claiming under 119(e) or 120 and may have adverse effects (e.g., on patent term).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain of benefit claims must specify relationship for each link
rubrics_metrics.description: Where benefit to multiple prior nonprovisional applications is claimed through a chain (e.g., A -> B -> C), the reference must identify all prior applications and indicate the relationship (continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part) between each nonprovisional application to establish copendency through the entire chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements that merely list application numbers without specifying the relationship for each link are improper. Each intermediate application must include appropriate references in its file to maintain the chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and formatting of multiple benefit claims in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If claiming the benefit of multiple prior applications, the references may be in a continuous string of multiple sentences at the beginning of the specification; these must begin as the first sentence after the title and not be separated by any other sentence not making a benefit claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any additional sentences including a benefit claim must immediately follow the first sentence and be contiguous; otherwise the claim may not be recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period to submit specific reference for certain applications (four months/16 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: For utility/plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on/after Nov 29, 2000, the specific reference must be submitted during pendency and within the later of four months from the actual filing date or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior application (similar rule for national stage filings after 35 U.S.C. 371).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time period is not extendable. Failure to submit the required reference within this period is considered a waiver of benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, and 365(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when specific reference is not timely filed (petition & surcharge)
rubrics_metrics.description: A benefit claim filed after the required time period may be accepted only if accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3) (or (a)(6) where applicable), the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.17(t), and a statement that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must include the required reference (unless previously submitted). The Director may require additional information to determine whether the delay was unintentional. If the reference was previously recognized on the filing receipt despite not being in the first sentence(s) or ADS, petition/surcharge may not be required but applicant must still amend the specification or file an ADS to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failing to be copending or to include proper reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A later-filed application that is not copending, or that does not contain the specific reference as required, is not entitled to the benefit of the prior application's filing date; prior art against its claims is determined from the later application's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office does not recognize a benefit claim because it lacks the required reference and the time for submitting it has expired, applicant must submit a petition and surcharge to accept an unintentionally delayed claim. The Office may not schedule publication based on an unrecognized earlier filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners should require insertion of missing references
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner is aware an application is a continuing application or that the applicant failed to submit the reference in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78(a), the examiner should call attention to this in an Office action using form paragraphs (e.g., 2.15 or 2.16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs exist (¶2.15, ¶2.16, etc.) to instruct applicants to add the specific reference in the required location. Do not require the applicant to make the reference in a CPA where such references are not permitted (CPA has its own requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA (continued prosecution application) specific-reference exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) is itself the specific reference required to every application assigned the same application number; therefore a specific reference in the first sentence(s) or ADS is not required and may not be made for applications assigned the same number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reference to an application not assigned the same application number but relied on for benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 must still be made. In a CPA, deletion of the specific reference to the prior application assigned the same number is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference after filing is ineffective to add benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference statement added after an application's filing date is not effective because no new matter can be added after filing; therefore an incorporation by reference in a post-filing amendment cannot be used to establish a benefit claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a benefit claim is submitted after filing, the reference to the prior application cannot include an incorporation by reference of the prior application unless such incorporation was presented upon filing. See Dart Indus. v. Banner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting or adding a benefit claim after filing often requires petition and may require additional filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not grant a corrected filing receipt to include a benefit claim unless the proper reference is included in the first sentence(s) or an ADS within the time required, with few exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adding after the time period, a petition and surcharge are required. Additionally, depending on application status, applicant may need to file an RCE (if under final rejection or allowed), a reissue application, or a request for certificate of correction if the application has issued as a patent. Amendments adding benefit claims near projected publication dates may not be recognized in time to affect publication scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of benefit claims and effects on patent term and prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may cancel their claim to priority by amending the specification or submitting a new ADS to delete references to prior applications; deletion may be used to avoid measuring patent term from an earlier date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider whether deletion makes new prior art available. Deleting a benefit claim after final rejection/allowance is treated under 37 CFR 1.116/1.312 respectively. Cancellation may be considered an intentional waiver, and a later petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim may be refused if benefit was intentionally cancelled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and examiner wording for improper benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraphs (e.g., ¶2.09, ¶2.11, ¶2.11.01, ¶2.15, ¶2.16) to indicate improper or missing benefit claims and instruct applicants what to delete or insert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ¶2.11 instructs deletion of a prior nonprovisional reference unless copendency can be established; ¶2.11.01 addresses failure to file within 12 months for provisional benefit. Examiner notes indicate bracket insertions (e.g., application number) and special-use rules (e.g., do not use certain paragraphs for 119(e) provisional claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to specify relationship when claiming benefit from multiple prior applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming the benefit of more than one nonprovisional application, the relationship between each application (continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part) must be specified to establish copendency throughout the entire chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper example: “this application claims the benefit of Application Nos. C, B, and A” is insufficient. Proper example: “this application is a continuation of Application No. C, filed ---, which is a continuation of Application No. B, filed ---, which is a continuation of Application No. A, filed ---.”
